facts.statement: Fossils of Austriadactylus were found in Late Triassic rocks in Austria dating to about 215 million years ago.
facts.quote: The fossil remains were unearthed in Late Triassic (middle Norian age, about 215 million years ago) rocks of Austria.

facts.statement: The genus Austriadactylus was named in 2002 by Fabio Marco Dalla Vecchia and colleagues.
facts.quote: The genus was named in 2002 by Fabio Marco Dalla Vecchia and colleagues.

facts.statement: Austriadactylus had an elongated skull measuring 11 cm in length.
facts.quote: The elongated skull has a length of 11 cm.

facts.statement: The skull featured a bony crest that widened toward the snout, reaching a height of 2 cm.
facts.quote: It carried a bony crest that widened as it descended towards the snout, up to a height of 2 cm.

facts.statement: Austriadactylus was heterodont, possessing teeth of different shapes.
facts.quote: The teeth differ in shape, and the species was thus heterodont.

facts.statement: Unlike other basal pterosaurs, Austriadactylus had a flexible tail without stiffening rod-like vertebral extensions.
facts.quote: The flexible tail did not have the stiffening rod-like vertebral extensions present in other basal pterosaurs.

facts.statement: The estimated wingspan of Austriadactylus is 120 cm.
facts.quote: The wingspan has been estimated at 120 cm.

facts.statement: Dental microwear analysis suggests Austriadactylus primarily ate hard invertebrates.
facts.quote: The dental microwear textures of Austriadactylus provide indications that the diet of the genus primarily consisted of hard invertebrates.

facts.statement: Originally placed in Pterosauria incertae sedis, later analyses placed Austriadactylus in the family Campylognathoididae related to Campylognathoides and Eudimorphodon.
facts.quote: Austriadactylus was in 2002 assigned by the describers to a general Pterosauria incertae sedis, but some later analyses showed it to have been related to Campylognathoides and Eudimorphodon in the Campylognathoididae.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Austriadactylus is a distinct genus or a junior synonym of Eudimorphodon.
facts.quote: It has even been suggested it was a junior synonym of Eudimorphodon, though perhaps a distinct species in that genus.

facts.statement: Austriadactylus lived during the Norian stage of the Late Triassic, between 215.38 and 205.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Norian to Norian (215.38 to 205.7 million years ago)
